Metadata.title: Celoria - AI-Powered Management for Salon Chains
Metadata.description: AI takes over the busywork — reconciliation, reports, marketing — so your managers can focus on what matters: great service.

Hero.description: AI takes over reconciliation, reports, and marketing — so your store managers can focus on service and your best stores' standards replicate everywhere.

Problem.title: Managing salon chains fails at three things. Every existing tool falls short.
Problem.card1Desc: In the U.S. nail industry, 79% are immigrant workers (UCLA Labor Center) with limited formal education. They can't read English UIs, let alone complex dashboards — they call daily asking how to operate. No existing tool is designed for this workforce.
Problem.card2Desc: Your best people spend hours on reconciliation, reports, and scheduling instead of serving clients and training staff. The more stores you open, the worse it gets.
Problem.card3Title: SOPs fail to replicate across stores
Problem.card3Desc: Huge efficiency gaps between best and worst stores. SOPs rely on memory; new stores drift immediately. Operational knowledge is locked in the owner's head.
Problem.callout: The problem isn't your people — it's that they're drowning in admin work. Celoria automates the busywork so your managers can get back to doing what they're good at: running a great store.

Solution.title: Two-layer product, each solving different problems.
Solution.subtitle: Staff don't need to learn software. Managers don't need to do paperwork.
Solution.staffDesc: Staff don't need to learn software. The system pushes tasks via Mobile App: "What to do + when to do it."
Solution.staffItem1: Detects idle slots → coordinates Marketing Agent, posts flash deals to fill gaps
Solution.staffItem2: Running a promo → pushes scripts + required actions to staff
Solution.staffItem3: VIP guest arrives → reminds staff to nurture relationship, offer extra service
Solution.staffCallout: Booking, scheduling, checkout still use GUI — keep simple things simple.
Solution.ownerDesc: AI handles the admin so your managers focus on clients and staff.
Solution.ownerItem2: Financial reconciliation → auto-executed, only reports anomalies
Solution.ownerItem3: Staff training → auto-generates materials when issues found
Solution.ownerItem4: Precision marketing → targets based on booking + guest data
Solution.ownerCallout: Your managers stay on the floor. You see everything from your phone.

AIVision.title: 5 AI assistants that work 24/7 across all your stores
AIVision.subtitle: Each one replaces a job you're either paying too much for, or doing yourself at midnight.
AIVision.orchestratorDesc: See all stores at a glance · Compare performance · Push changes everywhere at once
AIVision.agent1Desc: Spots trends you'd miss · Compares stores · Tells you what to fix and why
AIVision.agent2Desc: Fills empty slots · Sends targeted offers · Runs campaigns automatically
AIVision.agent3Desc: Pushes tasks to staff · Checks if SOPs are followed · No more repeating yourself
AIVision.agent4Desc: Closes the books daily · Flags discrepancies · No more manual spreadsheets
AIVision.agent5Desc: Generates training materials · Tracks performance · Optimizes schedules
AIVision.callout1Text: Rules-based — consistent and reliable, every single day
AIVision.callout2Text: AI-driven — handles the judgment calls that used to require a GM

Traction.title: 35 stores run on Celoria every day.
Traction.callout: NYC's largest nail chain switched to Celoria. 35 stores, 301 technicians, $98K+ daily revenue — all managed through one system, in both English and Chinese.
Traction.quote: 18 years in the industry, 50 stores. Our previous platform couldn't solve our real problems — staff couldn't use it, managers spent hours on reconciliation, and marketing was all manual. We needed a system built for how we actually work.
Traction.quoteAttribution: — Joey Fei, Owner of NYC's largest nail chain

Competitive.title: Other platforms give you dashboards. We give you answers.
Competitive.colAI: AI That Actually Works For You
Competitive.zenotiAI: 6 separate AI tools, don't talk to each other
Competitive.celoriaMultilingual: Native bilingual (EN/ZH) — UI + docs + native support
Competitive.celoriaAI: 5 AI assistants that work together — Insights · Marketing · SOPs · Reconciliation · Training
Competitive.footnote: Other platforms add features one by one. Celoria's AI was designed from day one to connect everything — scheduling, payments, marketing, and staff management all feed into smarter decisions.

BusinessModel.title: Three-layer revenue structure.
BusinessModel.tier1Desc: $20 base + $10/person — capped at $149/store. Scheduling, booking, POS, CRM, reports, multilingual — all basics included.
BusinessModel.tier2Desc: $99/location/month — Insights, auto-reconciliation, training generation, precision marketing. vs. $120K/yr GM, decisions in seconds.
BusinessModel.footnote: Based on 20 staff, $50K/mo revenue per location. AI + server cost ~$48/mo. Per-customer ARPU: ~$2,300/mo (avg 4-5 stores).

Moats.title: Triple compound moat.
Moats.moat1Desc: Every owner confirmation, rejection, and annotation trains the system. Competitors know "what happened" — we know "why." 50 stores × 365 days of decision data — non-replicable.
Moats.moat2Desc: Staff depend on the Digital Store Manager for daily work. SOPs, scripts, workflows all live in the system, not in people's heads. Leaving = losing all operational knowledge.
Moats.moat3Desc: Within brand: cross-store data drives precision marketing and deep Insights. Industry-level: more brands served → stronger baselines → new customers work out of the box.
Moats.calloutText: Supply chain recommendations and merchant financing (Toast Capital model) — revenue-based credit underwriting from the operational data we already collect.

Insight.quote: The middle layer — the GM who sits between data and decisions — doesn't need to be a person. An AI agent can monitor 50 stores in real time, detect anomalies, and deliver actionable insights directly to the owner — the person who actually knows what to do with them.
Insight.supportingText: GM says "significant growth." AI says "$5,080 — here's the list." All numbers derived from 77,921 real appointments — not guesses, just math.

WhyNow.title: YC is batch-investing in "vertical AI OS."
WhyNow.card1Desc: Bravi (home services), Carma (fleet management), Sandra AI (car dealerships), Tensol (hospitality), Brickanta (construction) — YC is funding the same thesis across verticals. The beauty vertical is still wide open.
WhyNow.card2Desc: We started from a blank page in 2024. Zenoti's Agents know what happened, but not why. Celoria's Agents participate in decisions — push recommendations, record every confirmation and rejection. The longer it runs, the better it understands each owner's management logic.
WhyNow.calloutText: Legacy SaaS features can be caught up. But AI-native architecture requires a full rewrite. The next 2–3 years will determine who owns the operational data layer for service businesses.

Team.title: Built by an Operator

Team.member2Bio: 18 years in the beauty industry. QQ Nails — NYC's largest nail salon chain. 35 stores live, first customer. Nail equipment supplier covering 100+ salons = built-in distribution channel.
Team.member3Bio: Amazon Senior Software Engineer — weekly architecture reviews, 6+ months. Senior SDE at major SaaS company — weekly engineering guidance. Veteran practitioners in Joey's industry network — product validation, market strategy.
